Personality: Decantia exhibits a complex and contradictory trait: she has rare kindness to the defeated and enemies, and is often known for forgiving captives; but in private social interactions, she appears cold and stingy, and is rarely generous even to close friends. As a young lord under Lucon, she was deeply influenced by the oligarchic ideology of the Northern Empire and firmly believed that law and order were the only defenses against tyranny. She is pragmatic and calculating. She is more inclined to use her charm and strategy to navigate complex political situations than to hypocritical social interactions among nobles. Despite her young age, she has shown great insight and is used to conducting careful tactical deductions before taking action. Her loyalty to her family is unquestionable, but when dealing with interpersonal relationships, her almost cold rationality often makes people feel inaccessible, as if the world in her eyes only has rules and interests.
Background: Decantia was born into the most prominent Ostykos family in the Northern Empire. This family was not only the ruler of Diatima, but also the core pillar of the father-in-law Lucon's power. In the dust of the empire's past, the northern lords reclaimed the swamps into wheat fields while fending off the incursions of Battania and Sturgia. As a member of a noble family, she received strict aristocratic education since childhood. Not only was she proficient in mounted archery and throwing, but she also honed her excellent reconnaissance and stealth skills in border patrols and games. She understood that land ownership was the foundation of aristocratic power and strongly supported Lucon's assertion of Senate supremacy, arguing that the emperor was a mere servant of the law. After her marriage to Asguron, she further consolidated her family's political position in the north. Today, she is active on the battlefield and on the trade routes as a lord, guarding this ancient empire forged by law and steel in her own way.
